declarations.description:
A camera viewfinder for taking a photo of a document, a card or a face, as in a bank's cheque deposit, an identity
check (KYC) or a receipt scanner. It shows the camera with a framing guide, tells the user what is wrong with the
picture (too dark, glare, moving, blurry), can take the photo by itself once the picture holds steady, and lets the
user retake or keep each photo. A list of required shots (`shots`: front of the card, back, a selfie) walks the user
through them in order. Each photo is handed over as a `Blob`.

The camera does not open on its own: the user presses **Start camera** (the browser then asks for permission), or
the app calls `start()`, or sets `autostart`. It closes when every photo is taken, on `stop()`, and when the element
leaves the page. The front camera is shown mirrored, as a mirror is; the photo is not. Without a camera, or with
access refused, the error screen says why and offers to try again. A camera needs a secure page (HTTPS).

`streamSource` replaces `getUserMedia` (a chosen device, a WebRTC stream, a canvas in a demo or a test), and
`assessFrame` replaces the built-in quality rules.

slots.description: Replaces the screen shown before the camera starts (an icon, a sentence and the Start camera button). Call `start()` from your own button.
slots.name: idle

slots.description: Replaces the screen shown when the camera cannot start. Read the reason from the `camera-error` event.
slots.name: error

slots.description: Replaces the drawing of the framing guide; the guide's box (`part="guide"`) stays, and is the area `crop` keeps.
slots.name: guide

slots.description: Action zone beside the shutter, for the app's own commands: upload a file instead, cancel.
slots.name: actions

slots.description: Replaces the summary shown once every photo is taken (the photos, each with a Retake button). The events do not bubble: listen on the element itself.
slots.name: done

members.name: guide
members.description: The framing guide: `none`, `document`, `card` or `face`. A shot of `shots` may choose its own.

members.name: facing
members.description: The camera to open: `environment` (the back one, the default) or `user` (the front one). Switching camera updates it.

members.name: shots
members.description:
The photos to take, in order: `[{ "id": "front", "label": "Front of the card", "guide": "card" }, …]`. As an
attribute, JSON. Empty takes a single photo. Setting a list with other content starts it over; the same content
again (a framework re-rendering a new array literal) changes nothing.

members.name: autoCapture
members.description: Takes the photo by itself once the picture has no problem and holds steady for `steady-time`. The shutter still works.

members.name: steadyTime
members.description: How long, in milliseconds, the picture must hold steady before auto-capture takes it.

members.name: crop
members.description: Keeps only the area inside the guide in the photo. Without it, the photo is the camera's whole frame.

members.name: imageType
members.description: The image format of the photos. A browser that cannot write it gives PNG.

members.name: imageQuality
members.description: The quality of a JPEG or WebP photo, from 0 to 1.

members.name: autostart
members.description: Opens the camera as soon as the element is on the page, without waiting for the Start camera button.

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the component. Empty uses the built-in "Camera".

members.name: streamSource
members.description: Supplies the video stream instead of `getUserMedia`. Set it before the camera starts.

members.name: assessFrame
members.description: Decides the quality hint of each sampled frame instead of the built-in rules (assessFrame).

members.name: openFacing
members.description: The camera actually open: `facing`, or the shot's own.

members.name: status
members.description: Where the component is: `idle`, `starting`, `live`, `review`, `done` or `error`. Also a custom state, `:state(live)`.

members.name: photos
members.description: The photos kept so far, in the order of the shots.

members.name: stream
members.description: The open camera's stream, for an app that also records or analyses it; null while the camera is closed.

members.name: start
members.description: Opens the camera. Does nothing while it is open or opening, under review or finished.

members.name: stop
members.description: Closes the camera and goes back to the idle screen, keeping the photos taken.

members.name: capture
members.description: Takes the photo now. Resolves with it, or `undefined` when the camera shows no picture.

members.name: retake
members.description: Throws the photo under review away and goes back to the camera; or, once finished, takes shot `index` again.

members.name: accept
members.description: Keeps the photo under review and moves on to the next shot still missing, or finishes.

members.name: switchCamera
members.description: Switches between the front and the back camera.

members.name: reset
members.description: Closes the camera and forgets every photo: the list starts over.

members.name: lost
members.description: The camera went away while open: unplugged, permission revoked, or taken by another application.

members.name: guideRegion

type.text: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number } | undefined

members.description:
The guide's box in the video's own pixels. The video fills the stage with `object-fit: cover`, so the box is
mapped through that scale and offset, and mirrored back for the front camera.

members.name: sample
members.description: Samples one frame for the hints and auto-capture, then schedules the next while the camera is live.

events.description: Fired when the camera shows its first picture.
events.name: camera-start

events.description: Fired when the camera cannot start, or stops while open (`ended`: unplugged, permission revoked); `kind` says why.
events.name: camera-error

events.description: Fired when a photo is taken, before the user keeps or retakes it. `detail.blob` is the image.
events.name: capture

events.description: Fired when the user throws a photo away to take it again.
events.name: retake

events.description: Fired when the user keeps a photo.
events.name: accept

events.description: Fired once every shot has a photo kept; the camera then closes.
events.name: complete
